privacy.metaDescription: How Gecko Cabane, a French-Thai restaurant in Krabi, collects and protects your personal data (Thai PDPA B.E. 2562 and GDPR).
privacy.title: Privacy policy

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Gecko Cabane, a French-Thai restaurant at Maharat Road, Krabi Town, Thailand. We are responsible for the personal data you give us through this website.

data.title: What we collect
data.body: When you request a reservation, we collect:
data.item4: your booking details: date, time, number of guests and occasion, if any;
data.item5: if you tick the box, your consent to receive our news, recorded with the date, the source and the version of the consent text;
data.item6: technical anti-abuse data, stored only as irreversible hashes and deleted after 2 days;
data.item7: if you use the "Something wrong?" form on the review page: your message and, if you provide it, your email address, sent by email to the restaurant and not stored on the website.

purpose.title: Why we use it
purpose.item3: send you our newsletter, only if you ticked the consent box. We never sell your data.

newsletter.title: Newsletter
newsletter.body: Here is how our newsletter works and what we keep when you subscribe:
newsletter.item1: you can subscribe from the website footer, the pop-up, the bill QR code page, the WiFi page or the box on the reservation form;
newsletter.item2: double opt-in: nothing is sent until you click the confirmation link. We keep the date, source, language and version of the consent text (newsletter-2026-10-17);
newsletter.item3: Resend (transactional emails and newsletter) processes your address on our behalf, only to send emails;
newsletter.item4: to tailor our messages, we keep your language, your country, whether you live in Krabi (box ticked or Thai number) and the date of your last visit. The country comes from your phone number if you booked, otherwise from an approximate location based on the network, for sign-ups made on the website only: only the country is kept and the IP address is not stored. Sign-ups made at the restaurant from the bill QR code or the WiFi page do not use network location, because it would always show Thailand;
newsletter.item5: the pop-up remembers in your browser for 90 days that it was shown (no identifier);
newsletter.item6: at most one newsletter a month, apart from the welcome email and the post-visit emails. Every email has an unsubscribe link, and unsubscribing is recorded immediately;
newsletter.item7: legal basis: your consent, under PDPA B.E. 2562 and the GDPR. You can withdraw it at any time.

rights.title: Legal basis and your rights
rights.body: We handle your reservation to carry out your request, and send the newsletter based on your consent. Under Thailand's Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA B.E. 2562) and the GDPR, you have the right to:
rights.item5: withdraw your consent at any time, without giving a reason;
rights.item6: lodge a complaint with the competent data protection authority.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: We keep your data only as long as needed:
retention.item1: reservation data: 24 months after your visit;
retention.item2: newsletter consent: until you withdraw it;

sharing.title: Who we share it with
sharing.body: Your data is never sold. It is processed by service providers, by category:
sharing.item4: audience measurement without cookies (Plausible Analytics): page views and clicks, without any personal identifier, hosted in the European Union.

contact.title: Exercising your rights and unsubscribing
contact.body: To exercise your rights or withdraw your consent, email us at geckocabanerestaurant@gmail.com or message us on WhatsApp at +66 81 958 5945. Every newsletter will include an unsubscribe link.

romanticDinner.subtitle: A small dining room, a French-Thai kitchen and an unhurried evening for two.
romanticDinner.heroAlt: The Gecko Cabane sign on Maharat Road in Krabi Town

ambiance.title: A quiet room for two
ambiance.p1: Gecko Cabane seats 40 guests at most, so the dining room stays calm and conversation comes easily. It is run by a French-Thai couple who welcome you themselves.
ambiance.p2: There is no show and no rush. You come for the food, a glass of wine or a Belgian beer, and time to talk. We are open every day, and the kitchen takes orders until 10 pm.

table.title: What you will eat
table.alt: Beef bourguignon served at Gecko Cabane
table.p1: The menu is French home cooking, such as beef bourguignon braised slowly in red wine, and chicken in a cream sauce. A few Thai dishes from the chef sit alongside, like a mild massaman curry.
table.p2: A short list of wines and Belgian beers goes with the meal. Ask us what works with your dishes; we are glad to help you choose.

chef.title: Cooked by Chef Jariya
chef.alt: Chef Jariya of Gecko Cabane in Krabi Town
chef.p1: Chef Jariya runs the kitchen and her French husband looks after the dining room. Together they have built a small restaurant they would want to eat in themselves.
chef.p2: If you are curious about a dish, just ask. They are happy to explain what is in it and how it is cooked.

occasion.title: Celebrating something?
occasion.p1: The booking form has an "Occasion" field. If it is an anniversary, a birthday or a first trip together, write it there and we will know when you arrive.

whereToEat.h1: Where to eat in Krabi Town
whereToEat.subtitle: A short guide to the night market, Walking Street and the river, and where to sit down for dinner.
whereToEat.heroAlt: The entrance of Gecko Cabane on Maharat Road in Krabi Town

intro.title: Eating well in a small town
intro.p1: Krabi Town is compact, so you can eat your way around it on foot. Most of what travellers enjoy here is simple and local: street food at a market, a seafood supper by the water, a sweet snack on a walk.
intro.p2: This page is not a ranking. It describes the places and habits that make an evening in town easy, so you can plan it your own way.

areas.title: Three places to start
areas.p1: These are areas rather than addresses. Walk around, look at what is cooking and choose what appeals to you.

c1.title: The night market
c1.text: Stalls with grilled skewers, noodles, fried snacks, fruit and Thai sweets. Come hungry, share a few plates and pay as you go.

c2.title: Walking Street
c2.text: The pedestrian street is usually busiest on weekend evenings, with food stalls, small shops and music. Check locally for the days it runs.

c3.title: The riverfront
c3.text: A calm place for a stroll at dusk, with seafood and Thai dishes served along the water. A good way to end a day of sightseeing.

when.title: What to try and when to go
when.p1: Look for grilled seafood, stir-fried dishes, green and red curries, som tam and mango with sticky rice. Markets are at their liveliest in the early evening, and it is usually cooler and calmer after sunset.
when.p2: Opening days and hours change with the season and the weather, so check locally on the day. Bring small notes and a little patience, and ask before you add chilli if you prefer mild food.

dinner.title: When you want to sit down for dinner
dinner.alt: A massaman curry served at Gecko Cabane
dinner.p1: After the market, some evenings call for a table, a menu and a quiet room. Gecko Cabane is a 40-seat restaurant on Maharat Road serving French and Thai dishes, cooked by Chef Jariya.
dinner.p2: We are open every day and the kitchen takes orders until 10 pm. You can book a table online in under a minute.

whereToEat.closingTitle: Plan your evening in Krabi Town

gettingHere.h1: Getting to Krabi Town from Ao Nang
gettingHere.subtitle: Staying in Ao Nang and fancy dinner in Krabi Town? Here is how to get to us and how to find the door.
gettingHere.heroAlt: The entrance of Gecko Cabane on Maharat Road in Krabi Town

overview.title: From the beach to town for dinner
overview.p1: Ao Nang and Krabi Town are separate places, and the ride between them takes a little planning. Many guests make the trip for an evening out, and it is an easy one once you know your options.
overview.p2: We do not run a shuttle, so this page describes the usual ways to travel. Fares and journey times change with traffic, season and the driver, so always agree the price before you set off.

options.title: Ways to get here
options.p1: Taxis, either metered or booked through a ride-hailing app, are the most direct choice. Shared songthaew pick-up trucks run along fixed routes and cost less, but they are slower and usually stop running early in the evening.
options.p2: A private transfer arranged through your hotel gives you a set price and a driver who waits or returns at a time you choose. If you are comfortable on two wheels, a rented scooter works too, though the road is busy after dark.
options.p3: Our suggestion is simple: book a ride with the Grab app and set the destination to "Gecko Cabane Restaurant", which you can find on Google Maps. The app shows the price and the estimated arrival time before you confirm, and the ride to Krabi Town is short and straightforward.

arrive.title: Finding us on Maharat Road
arrive.alt: The Gecko Cabane sign on Maharat Road in Krabi Town
arrive.p1: Gecko Cabane is on Maharat Road in the centre of Krabi Town. Show the driver the name of the street or open our location in your maps app.
arrive.p2: Look for the wooden sign and the entrance with plants out front. If you cannot find us, call the restaurant and we will guide you in.

back.title: Getting back after dinner
back.p1: Plan your ride back before the evening is over. Ask us about your ride back when you book, and we will tell you what we can suggest at that time.

wineBeer.h1: Wine and Belgian beer in Krabi Town
wineBeer.subtitle: A short guide to the wine and Belgian beer that goes with a French-Thai dinner.
wineBeer.heroAlt: Beef bourguignon served at Gecko Cabane in Krabi Town

intro.title: A short list, chosen to match the kitchen
intro.p1: A French kitchen and a glass of wine belong together, so Gecko Cabane keeps a short list of red, white and rosé wines chosen to suit the dishes on the menu.
intro.p2: The list is deliberately small. It is easier to choose from, and each bottle has a reason to be there.

belgian.title: Why Belgian beer
belgian.p1: Our kitchen is run by a French-Thai couple, and Belgian beer is a natural companion to French home cooking. Abbey-style ales, blonde ales and wheat beers share the table well with braised and creamy dishes.
belgian.p2: If you prefer beer to wine, ask us which style suits your dish. We are happy to explain the differences.

pairings.title: What goes with what
pairings.p1: These are suggestions, not rules. Choose what you enjoy.

c1.title: Beef bourguignon
c1.text: Slow-braised in red wine, it suits a red wine or an abbey-style ale with some depth.

c2.title: Chicken in cream sauce
c2.text: A rich, creamy sauce goes well with a dry white wine or a light blonde ale.

c3.title: Massaman curry
c3.text: The gentle spice and sweetness of a mild curry pair with a rosé or a wheat beer.

c4.title: Velvety soup
c4.text: A smooth soup to start works with a crisp white wine or a blonde ale.

list.title: See the full list
list.p1: The complete list of wines and beers, with current prices, is on our menu page.
